say.text: The Mini R C bench is a pocket tester for speed controllers and servos. This video walks through every screen of firmware 0.1.0, in 12 chapters.
It starts with a splash that stays for 3 seconds. The amber line says: unplug any servo from G-P 0 now. D shot starts on that pin right after the splash.
Then the tester opens. With no speed controller connected it reads no telemetry, and every tile shows two dashes.

title.heading:
Every screen of
the MiniRcBench
title.text: ESC tester, telemetry, ESC settings, servo tester, servo programmers, S.BUS monitor, angle meter, SD log, settings. 12 chapters.

labels.title: UNPLUG ANY SERVO FROM GP0 NOW
labels.text: DShot starts on the signal pin after the 3 s splash. A servo reads it as a pulse.

labels.title: NO TELEMETRY
labels.text: No ESC answers: -- in the six tiles, a dark red zero for the RPM.

say.text: Chapter 1, the tester. It drives one speed controller over bidirectional D shot. The large number is the motor's R P M, worked out from the electrical R P M and the pole count.
The top row holds the state, safe or armed, the D shot rate, the state of the card, and the voltage of the bench's own cell.
Arming takes a hold of 1 second on hold to arm, with the throttle at zero. A green bar fills along the badge while the finger stays down.
Armed, the badge is red. The bar sets the throttle. Its full width is the ceiling, 20 percent by default. Here the bar gives 13 percent.
The area above the bar is a swipe pad for fine steps. Latch keeps the throttle where the finger leaves it. Disarm acts on touch, not on release.
While armed, the line under the number reads R P M per volt. From 75 percent throttle on, an estimate of the motor's kV appears: 1758 in this picture.
A speed controller set to 3 D mode gets a note on the tester: from zero to 50 percent the motor runs reversed.

Three interlocks stop a motor on their own. 30 seconds without a touch disarm the tester. Opening the menu disarms it. And when the display stalls for 250 milliseconds, the second processor core sets the throttle to zero.

labels.title: RPM
labels.text: RPM = eRPM / (poles / 2). 14 poles by default; a tap on the pole count opens SETTINGS.

labels.title: BOARD 3.92 V
labels.text: The bench's own cell, not the ESC's battery. The ESC's voltage is in the VOLTAGE tile.

labels.title: HOLD TO ARM
labels.text: 1 s hold, throttle at zero for at least 250 ms.

labels.title: Throttle bar
labels.text: Full width = MAX, the ceiling: 20 % by default, 5 % to 100 % in SETTINGS.

labels.title: DISARM acts on touch
labels.text: Every other control acts when the finger lifts. LATCH off sets the throttle to zero.

labels.title: RPM/V and KV EST
labels.text: RPM/V 1400 at 79 % throttle, KV EST 1758: RPM × 2000 / (voltage × throttle).

labels.title: 3D MODE ESC
labels.text: 0 to 50 % reversed at twice the step, above 50 % the set way.

labels.title: Three interlocks
labels.text:
Idle disarm after 30 s, with a countdown over the last 5 s.
MENU disarms.
Heartbeat: throttle zero after 250 ms.

say.text: Chapter 2, telemetry. Six tiles. Voltage, current, temperature, stress and status come as extended D shot telemetry, E-D-T, on the signal wire itself. No third wire is needed.
Status reads O K in green, a warning in amber, an error in red. The link tile counts the answers per second and the error rate: 998 per second with zero percent errors is a clean link.
With a KISS telemetry wire on the second pin, the tags change to KISS. The steps are then a hundredth of a volt and of an ampere, and the used milliamp hours appear.
A value that is not refreshed for 1 second turns into dashes. An expired status never reads O K.
The top row also shows the card: S D, a red rec while a log runs, no S D, or an amber chip after a write error.

labels.title: EDT
labels.text: Extended DShot telemetry. Steps of 0.25 V and 1 A. The bench switches it on by itself.

labels.title: LINK 998/S, 0% ERR
labels.text: A clean 1 kHz link. The error rate turns amber above 5 %: set DSHOT to 300.

labels.title: KISS
labels.text: A third wire on AUX, 115200 baud, 50 frames/s. Steps of 0.01 V and 0.01 A, and the used mAh.

labels.title: Expired
labels.text: EDT values after 1 s, the RPM after 500 ms without an answer.

labels.title: SD, REC, NOSD, SDERR
labels.text: The state of the microSD card and of the log.

say.text: Chapter 3, the menu. Eight rows: commands and config for the speed controller, servo tester, servo programmer, receiver signals, tools, S D log and settings. The list scrolls under a finger.
The strip on top names the two pins and the D shot rate. The chip beside it says what the speed controller answers: E-D-T on, a red E-D-T off, or no speed controller.
Dragged up, the last two rows carry a state: the card's, and settings that are not saved yet, in amber.
When a tool hands the signal pin back, D shot restarts, and the rows are outlines for that moment.
After a settings session an amber line asks for a power cycle of the speed controller. It stays until the motor's R P M answers again.

labels.title: 8 rows
labels.text: ESC COMMANDS, ESC CONFIG, SERVO TESTER, SERVO PROGRAMMER, RX SIGNALS, TOOLS, SD LOG, SETTINGS.

labels.title: EDT ON, EDT OFF, NO ESC
labels.text: EDT OFF: the ESC sends its RPM, but no extended telemetry.

labels.title: READY, UNSAVED
labels.text: SD LOG shows the card's state, SETTINGS shows UNSAVED or UPDATED.

labels.title: DSHOT RESTARTING
labels.text: The rows take no tap until DShot runs again.

labels.title: POWER-CYCLE THE ESC TO RUN IT
labels.text: The bench sends no start command to a bootloader.

say.text: Chapter 4, commands. Three things a speed controller takes as a D shot command: a beep, the direction of rotation, and 3 D mode.
Beep 1 to 5 finds a motor in a model. Direction and 3 D mode take a hold of 1 second. The bench sets the value, then sends the save command.
While a command goes out, the controls are outlines.
A speed controller sends no answer to a command. The screen says so, and tells you to check the result on the tester.
With no speed controller answering, nothing is sent.

labels.title: ESC COMMANDS
labels.text: DShot commands, sent only while the tester is disarmed and the motor stands.

labels.title: HOLD 1 S
labels.text: NORMAL, REVERSED, 3D OFF and 3D ON are set and then saved in the ESC.

labels.title: SENDING 3 (BEEP 3)
labels.text: One command at a time.

labels.title: No answer to a command
labels.text: The bench cannot confirm the setting. The tester shows the 3D note until a restart or 3D OFF.

labels.title: NO ESC ANSWERS ON SIG GP0
labels.text: All controls are outlines.

say.text: Chapter 5, config. Two entries. Settings reads and writes the settings of A-M 32, Bluejay and BLHeli_S speed controllers. The U-S-B bridge is for a desktop tool on a computer.

Settings talks to the bootloader, and a bootloader listens only briefly at power-up. So the screen asks: power-cycle the speed controller. Unplug its battery and plug it in again while this screen is open.
Then the list. The strip names the controller and its firmware, here A-M 32 version 2.16. The rows scroll under a finger.
Tap a row to edit it. Minus and plus make fine steps, a sideways swipe a coarse one. A changed value turns cyan, and revert takes every change back.
Write opens a page that lists every change and still writes nothing. With a card in the slot, the old settings go into a backup file first. Then: hold to write, for 1 second.
The bench reads the settings back and compares every byte. Write verified, in green. A power cycle of the speed controller applies them.
Hex shows the raw bytes. A settings layout the bench does not know opens in this view only, and cannot be written.
Bluejay and BLHeli_S open the same way. Their write has run against a simulated speed controller only, not against a real one.
Back opens a leave page: unplug the battery, then leave. The bench writes settings only. It does not update a speed controller's firmware.
For that there is the U-S-B bridge. It passes a tool on a computer through to the speed controller's bootloader. The bench waits for the tool's first byte.
That byte picks the mode: plain passthrough, or the 4-way interface, in which the bench answers like a flight controller. A motor command from the computer is refused.

labels.title: ESC SETTINGS, USB BRIDGE
labels.text: Settings on the bench itself, or a computer's tool passed through.

labels.title: POWER-CYCLE THE ESC
labels.text: 19200 baud on the signal wire. 1 s of silence, then 3 handshakes per try.

labels.title: NEOESC F051, AM32 2.16
labels.text: What the ESC answered. Fields an older firmware does not read are hidden.

labels.title: Edit
labels.text: PWM FREQ from 24 kHz to 25 kHz. Nothing is written yet.

labels.title: HOLD TO WRITE
labels.text: 5 changes, backup BACKUP/AM001.TXT. Without the backup on the card, nothing is written.

labels.title: WRITE VERIFIED
labels.text: Read back 300 ms after the write, up to 3 tries.

labels.title: ESC HEX
labels.text: Layouts 2 to 4 are editable. Others are read-only and still get a backup.

labels.title: Bluejay, BLHeli_S
labels.text: Bluejay 0.21 and BLHeli_S 16.3 to 16.7 are editable.

labels.title: Leave page
labels.text: The bootloader waits for commands and may read DShot as one. Unplug first.

labels.title: USB BRIDGE: WAITING
labels.text: The board's serial port, 19200 baud on the signal pin. DShot is off.

labels.title: PASSTHROUGH or 4-WAY INTERFACE
labels.text: The bridge never spins the motor: MOTOR COMMAND FROM THE PC REFUSED.

say.text: Chapter 6, the servo tester. It sends servo pulses of 400 to 2500 microseconds, 50 to 560 times a second. It opens safe: the pin is low, there is no pulse, and the servo's supply is off.
Hold to start, for 1 second. The boost converter switches on, and the servo goes to centre.
Drag on the dial, or tap min, centre and max. The horn on the screen is the commanded position. The bench gets no feedback from the servo.
Sweep moves the servo to and fro and counts the moves. Speed slows every move, down to 10 percent, where the full travel takes 5 seconds. Stop acts on touch.
Set holds the profile: one or two servos, the type, the rate, the three pulse lengths, and the sweep's shape, rate, amplitude, dwell and count. Nothing of it is stored.
A heli type, or a rate above 60 hertz, waits for a second hold, because such a profile can destroy a servo that is not made for it.
With two servos, the second runs on the other pin. A, B, or both, and reverse B mirrors the second one.
With the current sensor fitted, the screen shows the supply's current and voltage: 0.42 ampere and 5.02 volts in this picture.
The sensor also cuts the supply: at 3 ampere, above 1 ampere for 400 milliseconds, which is a stalled servo, or under 4 volts for 1 second. A cut is not a fuse.
And it times a move: how long the servo took, the peak current and the holding current.
Back opens the leave page. Unplug the servo first, because a servo reads D shot on its pin as a pulse.

labels.title: SAFE
labels.text: No pulse. GP28 SUPPLY ON AT START: the boost converter is off until the hold.

labels.title: HOLD TO START
labels.text: 1 s. The supply counts as up at 4.5 V, or after 500 ms without a sensor.

labels.title: 1000 US
labels.text: The pulse the bench sends, not a measured position.

labels.title: SWEEP 1
labels.text: The sweep runs on the second core. STOP switches the pulses and the supply off.

labels.title: SERVO SET
labels.text: Types: STANDARD PWM, NARROW 760, WIDE, HELI CYCLIC, HELI TAIL 760. Sweep: SQUARE, SINE, TRIANGLE.

labels.title: HOLD TO APPLY
labels.text: 333 Hz and 1520 µs wait for a 1 s hold.

labels.title: A, B, AB
labels.text: A 1750 µs, B 1250 µs: mirrored by REVERSE B.

labels.title: 0.42 A, 5.02 V
labels.text: From the INA219, read 40 times a second.

labels.title: OVERCURRENT
labels.text: Cuts: 3.0 A in one reading, more than 1.0 A for 400 ms, less than 4.0 V for 1 s. A cut takes up to 60 ms.

labels.title: MOVE 0.45 S, PEAK 0.95 A, HOLD 0.12 A
labels.text: An upper bound at SPEED 100 %.

say.text: Chapter 7, the servo programmer. Three entries: KST and Chaservo, Hitec D series, and Hitec classic. With a switched supply, the bench powers the servo itself.
A KST servo answers only right after power-on. So the bench switches the supply off for 2 seconds, then on, and tries. It does that up to 14 times in 30 seconds.
Without a switched supply, the screen says when to power the servo up by hand.
Then the list: 27 fields in groups. Tune, pulse, failsafe, and a locked group in grey that is read-only.
Editing works as on the speed controller: tap, minus and plus, or a swipe. Here the dead band goes from 2.0 to 2.2 microseconds.
Write lists the change and names the backup file. Then hold to write. Each register is written and read back, and at the end everything is verified.
Write verified. When a write fails, the bench rolls back, and the screen says whether the servo holds its old values or is in doubt.
Files saves the settings to the card, loads a file as pending changes, and restores a backup.
The leave page switches the supply off. Hold to reboot restarts the servo with its new values.
Hitec D series servos have 20 parameters: speed, dead band, soft start, neutral and both ends, direction, failsafe, overload protection and more.
The steps are the same: edit, the write page, hold to write, with a backup on the card. Keep the horn clear.
The classic families, HS-5xxx and HS-7xxx, are read as well. A bad checksum shows in amber and can be repaired.

labels.title: PROGRAMMER
labels.text: SERVO SUPPLY GP28: the bench switches the 5 V. HITEC CLASSIC needs that.

labels.title: SWITCHED SUPPLY
labels.text: Off 2 s, on, one try. 14 power-ups in 30 s.

labels.title: POWER UP THE SERVO NOW
labels.text: One try about every 118 ms, for 30 s.

labels.title: 27 fields
labels.text: 32 registers, each read until 3 of 5 reads agree.

labels.title: DEAD BAND 2.0 → 2.2 US
labels.text: Cyan: changed, not yet written.

labels.title: HOLD TO WRITE
labels.text: 1 s. Backup BACKUP/KST001.TXT, record KST/KST.TXT.

labels.title: WRITE VERIFIED
labels.text: Other results: ROLLED BACK, NOTHING WAS WRITTEN, IN DOUBT. After IN DOUBT only a restore is accepted.

labels.title: KST FILES
labels.text: SAVE AS, LOAD, RESTORE. Up to 50 files.

labels.title: HOLD TO REBOOT
labels.text: A power cycle of the servo from the bench.

labels.title: HITEC SERVO: D485HW
labels.text: 21 registers, 115200 bit/s, half duplex on the signal wire.

labels.title: SPEED 100 % → 90 %
labels.text: KEEP THE SERVO HORN CLEAR: the servo may move on a write.

labels.title: CHECKSUM BAD, REPAIR
labels.text: Measured models: HS-5645MG and HS-7955TG. Others are written in the classic layout.

say.text: Chapter 8, receiver signals. Monitor is built. Output, S.BUS to a flight controller, is not built.
The monitor reads S.BUS from a receiver on G-P 1, at 100 kilobaud. The receiver runs on its own supply.
16 channels as bars, with their pulse lengths in microseconds. Below them: channels 17 and 18, the frame interval, 14 milliseconds here, and counters for lost frames and errors.
In failsafe the bars turn red. After 100 milliseconds of silence they turn grey.
Leaving asks to unplug the receiver before D shot restarts.

labels.title: MONITOR, OUTPUT
labels.text: OUTPUT is an outline: NOT BUILT.

labels.title: AUX GP1, 100 KBAUD, 8E2
labels.text: Inverted S.BUS, signal and ground only.

labels.title: FAILSAFE
labels.text: Chips: OK, FRAME LOST, FAILSAFE, NO SIGNAL.

say.text: Chapter 9, tools. One tool so far: the angle meter. It uses the motion sensor on the board, with no wire and no pin.
Lay the bench on a wing or a control surface. It shows the angle in tenths of a degree. Zero takes the present position as the reference, and max keeps the largest angle to each side.
With the surface's length set, it also gives the throw at the trailing edge: 13.7 millimetres for 20 degrees on 40 millimetres.
Flip cal calibrates the sensor in three poses. Treat a reading as a comparison between two surfaces, not as an exact angle.

labels.title: ANGLE METER
labels.text: Incidence, decalage, dihedral and control surface throw, from the QMI8658 accelerometer.
SETTLED: within 0.5° for 1 s. ZERO waits for a settled reading.

labels.title: −13.7 MM
labels.text: LENGTH 40 mm from hinge to trailing edge, set under SETUP: 10 to 500 mm.

say.text: Chapter 10, the S D log. With a card in the slot, arming starts a log and disarming stops it. Start and stop do the same by hand.
It records 500 frames per second in the Betaflight blackbox format, about 26 megabytes per hour. Dropped frames should stay at zero. This picture shows 3, in red.
After a stop the screen shows the run: highest R P M, current and temperature, lowest voltage, used capacity and armed time. The same goes into a text file beside the log.
U-S-B drive hands the card to a computer, read-only, so no card reader is needed. While the computer holds the card, arming is blocked.
The card is mounted at power-up. For a card that goes in later, press retry mount.

labels.title: SD LOG
labels.text: Files LOGS/LOGnnnnn.BFL on a FAT32 card.

labels.title: DROPPED FRAMES 3
labels.text: BUF PEAK turns amber above half of the 8192 bytes, red above three quarters.

labels.title: The run
labels.text: LOG00001.TXT beside LOG00001.BFL. A maximum counts after 3 readings in a row.

labels.title: USB DRIVE
labels.text: Refused while armed or recording. EJECT gives the card back.

labels.title: RETRY MOUNT
labels.text: The slot has no card-detect pin.

say.text: Chapter 11, settings. One list in sections. Motor poles and the throttle ceiling come first. The ceiling goes from 5 to 100 percent.
Wiring: the signal pin, the D shot rate from 150 to 1200, KISS telemetry, and the second pin. One step swaps the two pins, so they never share one.
Servo supply names the pin that switches the boost converter, or own, for a servo with a supply of its own. Current sense tells the bench that an INA219 is fitted. Found means: it answers.
Display: the backlight, and a high contrast theme for daylight.
At the end: the firmware version, the clock, the reason of the last restart, and the uptime. The board has no clock battery, so a computer sets the clock after each power-up.
Nothing is kept until hold to save. Until then an amber line reads unsaved. Hold defaults brings the defaults back.

labels.title: ESC TESTER
labels.text: MOTOR POLES 2 to 28, MAX THROTTLE 5 % to 100 % in steps of 5 %.

labels.title: WIRING
labels.text: SIG PIN, DSHOT 150 / 300 / 600 / 1200, KISS TELEM, AUX PIN.

labels.title: SERVO SUPPLY, CURRENT SENSE
labels.text: OWN, GP28 or GP29. NONE or INA219, with FOUND, NOT FOUND or OTHER PART.

labels.title: CONTRAST HIGH
labels.text: NORMAL or HIGH. BACKLIGHT 16 to 255.

labels.title: BOARD, DIAGNOSTICS
labels.text: LAST RESTART is amber for BROWN-OUT, GLITCH and WATCHDOG.

labels.title: HOLD TO SAVE
labels.text: 1 s. Writes all settings to flash.

say.text: Chapter 12, what all screens share. A tap acts when the finger lifts. Disarm and stop act on touch. Minus and plus repeat while held. And everything that writes, to a speed controller, a servo or the flash, takes a hold of 1 second.
When the bench's own cell is low, under 3.3 volts, a write is refused, so that it cannot stop halfway.

labels.title: One set of rules
labels.text:
Tap: on release.
DISARM, STOP: on touch.
− and +: repeat.
Writes: 1 s hold.

labels.title: BOARD VOLTAGE IS RED: NOT WRITTEN
labels.text: Below 3.30 V, until the cell is back at 3.35 V.

The menu and its state chips
ESC config: AM32, Bluejay, BLHeli_S, USB bridge
Servo tester: pulses, sweep, two servos, current cuts
SD log: blackbox, run summary, USB drive
scenes.say: That is every screen of the Mini R C bench. The manual in the project's wiki has the details.
